study_identification_part.si_4_title: Towards Longitudinal Characterization of Multiple Sclerosis Atrophy Employing SynthSeg Framework and Normative Modeling

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used 326 MS patients from 5 datasets: (1) MSSEG2016 - MICCAI 2016 challenge public dataset (N=53), (2) OpenMSLong - public dataset (N=20), (3) CHUV - in-house from Lausanne University Hospital (N=41), (4) NIL - in-house from Louvain Neuroinflammation Imaging Lab (N=47), (5) INsIDER - in-house Imaging Axonal Damage & Repair in MS dataset (N=165). Additionally, the CentileBrain normative model trained on 37,407 healthy individuals from 81 external datasets was used as the reference normative model (not trained in this study).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "We analyzed a heterogeneous dataset comprising 326 MS patients from five sources: three in-house datasets (Lausanne University Hospital (CHUV), Louvain Neuroinflammation Imaging Lab (NIL), and Imaging Axonal Damage & Repair in Multiple Sclerosis (INsIDER)) and two public datasets (MICCAI-MSSEG2016 challenge and OpenMSLong)." ... "the CentileBrain model trained with 37,407 healthy individuals (53.3% females, age range 3-90) from 81 datasets has been released."
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Gordaliza2024.pdf.md: Section 2.1 Materials, L49; Section 2.2 Methods / Normative Modeling, L73-75

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: This study did NOT train a new normative model. Instead, it used the pre-existing CentileBrain normative model as reference to assess subcortical volume deviations in MS patients. The 5 MS patient datasets were used as transfer/clinical application sets to evaluate individual deviations from normative healthy trajectories. OpenMSLong, CHUV, and INsIDER included longitudinal data for some subjects (total 460 scans from 326 patients).
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "By comparing subcortical volumes of 326 MS patients to a normative model from 37,407 healthy individuals, we identify significant deviations..." ... "The CentileBrain model employs Multivariate Factorial Polynomial Regression (MFPR) algorithm which performs robustly on healthy subjects, generating sex-specific normative models for the volume estimation of subcortical regions..."

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: This study did not train its own normative model. The CentileBrain model, which was pre-trained using 37,407 healthy individuals from 81 datasets, was used as an external reference. The specific train/validation/test split of CentileBrain is not reported in this paper but is described in the original CentileBrain publication (Ge et al. 2024, Lancet Digital Health).

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The paper reports that 53.3% of the 37,407 healthy individuals in CentileBrain were female. Female N = 37,407 × 0.533 = 19,938 (rounded to 19,937). Male N = 37,407 - 19,937 = 17,470. Male percentage = 100% - 53.3% = 46.7%. Train-phase breakdown is not reported in this paper.
